name: aids.1.student
description: No aids. You work by hand, without a calculator.

name: aids.1.model
description: Aids: This applies to Part 1 of the exam, where no aids are allowed. Expect the student to work by hand, without a calculator. The practice should reflect how the skill is actually to be carried out in the exam, under the aid rules that take effect in spring 2027 (no computer or tablet at all in Part 2 - only a simple scientific calculator, the student's own notes on paper, and printed aids).

name: aids.2.student
description: From spring 2027 this part is answered by hand. You may use a simple scientific calculator, your own notes on paper and printed aids — but no computer or tablet, and no graphing, equation-solving or programmable calculator.

name: aids.2.model
description: Aids: This applies to Part 2 of the exam, which from spring 2027 is to be answered by hand. Expect the student to use a simple scientific calculator (able to handle square roots, logarithms, sine/cosine/tangent and standard deviation), possibly together with their own notes and printed aids. Note: graphing calculators, and calculators that can solve equations, be programmed or communicate with other devices, are NOT permitted - nor is CAS software or a computer/tablet (e.g. GeoGebra). The practice should reflect how the skill is actually to be carried out in the exam, under the aid rules that take effect in spring 2027.

name: Find a percentage of a number
description: work out how much a given percentage of a number amounts to.
instruction: Give the student a number and a percentage, and ask them to find that percentage of the number. No context or interpretation required, only the calculation itself.

name: Convert between percentages, decimals and fractions
description: convert a number between percentage form, decimal form and fraction form.
instruction: Give the student numbers in one form (percentage, decimal or fraction) and ask them to convert to the other two. Purely mechanical practice.

name: Find the percentage change between two numbers
description: work out by how many per cent a value has increased or decreased, given the original and the new value directly (without being given a growth factor).
instruction: Give the student an original and a new value (e.g. an old and a new price) and ask them to find the percentage change. Pure calculation, a single numerical answer.

name: Find the growth factor from a percentage change
description: work out the growth factor given a percentage increase or decrease, and conversely find the percentage change from a given growth factor.
instruction: Give the student a percentage change and ask them to find the growth factor, or the other way round: given a growth factor, find the percentage change. Both directions should be practised.

name: Work out the result of several successive percentage changes
description: multiply several growth factors together to find the total change, and explain why the order and the size of the changes do not cancel each other out symmetrically.
instruction: Give the student two or more successive percentage changes (e.g. down 20 % then up 20 %) and ask them to find the total change, and to justify whether the result is higher than, lower than or equal to the starting point.

name: Interpret an expression containing several growth factors
description: read a mathematical expression made up of several growth factors (possibly with exponents) and explain in words which price development or change the expression describes.
instruction: Give the student an expression such as 1.05 · 0.85^2 and ask them to explain in words which percentage changes the expression represents, in the right order.

name: Calculate the price in a given year from a price index
description: work out the price of a good in a given year when the price in the base year and the index value are known.
instruction: Give the student the price in the base year and the index value for another year, and ask them to find the price in that other year. Pure calculation, a single numerical answer.

name: Convert between nominal and real wages using the CPI
description: use the consumer price index (CPI) for two different years to work out which nominal or real wage gives the same purchasing power.
instruction: Give the student the CPI for two years and a wage in one of them, and ask them to find the wage that gives the same purchasing power in the other year. This requires the student first to identify the right method (index calculation) and then to interpret what 'the same purchasing power' means.

name: Price index and base year
description: A price index compares the price level in different years against a chosen base year, and the index is always 100 in the base year.

name: Reverse a product of growth factors
description: interpret an expression in which a known value is divided by a product of several growth factors, and explain that this gives the value before those percentage changes took place.
instruction: Give the student an expression in which a known final value is divided by a product of two or more growth factors, and ask them to explain in words which price changes the expression reverses, and what the result of the calculation represents.

name: Convert between units of length
description: convert between units of length such as mm, cm, m and km.
instruction: Give the student a length in one unit (mm, cm, m or km) and ask them to convert it to another, stated unit. Pure conversion practice, no context needed.

name: Scale
description: The scale of a drawing is the ratio between a length on the drawing and the corresponding length in reality, expressed in the same unit on both sides.

name: Determine the scale of a drawing
description: determine the scale of a drawing given a length on the drawing and the corresponding length in reality.
instruction: Give the student a length on a drawing and the corresponding real length (in different units), and ask them to determine the scale in the form 1:n or n:1.

name: Use a scale to work out a length
description: use a given scale together with one known length (on the drawing/model or in reality) to work out the corresponding unknown length.
instruction: Give the student a scale (e.g. 1:1100) and one known length (in reality or on a model/drawing), and ask them to work out the corresponding unknown length.

name: Data sets and observations
description:
Observation: one single measurement or one single answer.
Data set: all the observations together. It is the data set that is sorted, and the observations that are sorted within it - ascending or descending.

name: Find the median of a data set
description: sort a data set and determine the median, both when the number of observations is odd and when it is even.
instruction: Give the student an unsorted data set (ideally with an odd number of values in one task and an even number in another) and ask them to determine the median. Require them to show the sorting.

name: Calculate the mean of a data set
description: calculate the mean (the arithmetic average) of a data set.
instruction: Give the student a data set and ask them to calculate the mean by hand (add up the values and divide by how many there are).

name: Determine the range
description: determine the range of a data set as the difference between the largest and the smallest value.
instruction: Give the student a data set and ask them to find the range.

name: Determine the mode
description: determine the mode of a data set - the value that occurs most often - and say when a data set has several modes, or none at all.
instruction: Give the student a data set and ask them to find the mode. Do include an example with two equally frequent values.

name: Frequency and relative frequency
description: Frequency is the number of times a value occurs in a data set, and relative frequency is the frequency expressed as a proportion (percentage) of the total number of observations.

name: Determine a relative frequency
description: determine the relative frequency of a given value in a data set, express it as a percentage, and give a practical interpretation of the answer in the context the task describes.
instruction: Give the student a concrete data set from a practical context and ask them to determine the relative frequency of one stated value, and then to explain in their own words what the answer means in that context.

name: Read and use a frequency table
description: read a frequency table, add up frequencies, and use the relationship between the total number of observations and the individual frequencies to determine or check a missing or claimed frequency.
instruction: Give the student a frequency table in which one frequency is missing or unknown, together with the total number of observations, and ask them to determine the missing frequency or to judge whether a claim about it holds.

name: Determine the mean and the median from a frequency table
description: determine the mean and the median of a data set given as a frequency table, by weighting each value by its frequency.
instruction: Give the student a frequency table (value and count) and ask them to determine the mean and the median for the whole data set, showing the working.

name: Cumulative frequency
description: The cumulative frequency for a value is the sum of the frequencies up to and including that value (possibly expressed as a percentage), and it can be used to answer questions of the type «how many / what proportion are at most or at least X».

name: Grouped data
description: A grouped data set is sorted into class intervals, and the frequency table only says how many observations fall in each interval. The individual observations are therefore lost: you know how many lie in a class, but no longer where in the class they lie.

name: Interpret a cumulative frequency graph
description: read off and explain what the coordinates of a given point on a cumulative frequency graph tell us about the underlying data.
instruction: Show the student a cumulative frequency graph with one point marked, and ask them to explain in their own words what the coordinates of that point tell us about the data (e.g. what proportion lies below a given value).

name: Estimate the median from a cumulative frequency graph
description: use a cumulative frequency graph to estimate the median of grouped data, and can account for the fact that this requires an assumption that the values are evenly (linearly) distributed within each class.
instruction: Show the student a cumulative frequency graph for grouped data and ask them to read off an estimate of the median, and to state explicitly which assumption they are making for that reading to be valid.

name: Determine the cumulative frequency for ungrouped data
description: determine the cumulative frequency (count or percentage) for a given value in an ungrouped data set, and give a practical interpretation of the answer.
instruction: Give the student a concrete, ungrouped data set (a frequency table works well) and ask them to determine the cumulative frequency for a stated value, with a practical interpretation in context. In Part 1 the counting is done by hand; in Part 2 a handheld calculator may be used for the counting and the percentages - but neither offers a shortcut around the reasoning itself.

name: Calculate the mean from grouped data
description: estimate the mean of a grouped data set by using the midpoint of each class to represent the values in that class, and explain that this rests on an assumption that the values are reasonably evenly distributed within each class.
instruction: Give the student a frequency table with grouped data and ask them to estimate the mean using the midpoint of each class, and to state explicitly which assumption the estimate rests on. This can be done by hand in Part 1 or with a calculator in Part 2.

name: Determine the proportion of a grouped data set above or below a given value
description: for a grouped data set, determine what proportion of the observations lies above or below a given value that does not necessarily fall on a class boundary, by assuming an even distribution within the class the value falls in.
instruction: Give the student a grouped frequency table and a particular value (e.g. a mean they have just calculated) that falls inside one of the classes, and ask them to estimate what proportion of the data set lies above or below that value.

name: Standard deviation
description: The standard deviation measures how much the values in a data set typically deviate from the mean, and a lower standard deviation means less spread.

name: Use the statistics mode on a calculator
description: enter a data set into the statistics mode of a handheld calculator and read off measures of centre such as the mean and the median.
instruction: Give the student a data set with a fairly large number of values and ask them to enter it into the statistics mode of the calculator and read off the mean and the median, and to compare this with a calculation by hand on a small subset of the numbers.

name: Determine the standard deviation of a data set
description: use a handheld calculator to determine the standard deviation of a data set, and explain what the value tells us about the spread.
instruction: Give the student a data set and ask them to use the calculator to find the standard deviation, and then to explain briefly what the value tells us about the spread in this particular data set.

name: Compare distributions from measures of centre and spread
description: reason about the shape and the spread of two distributions from stated measures of centre (mean, median) and spread (standard deviation), without knowing the original data.
instruction: Give the student measures of centre and spread for two data sets (without the data themselves) and ask them to describe what the differences tell us about how the two distributions probably look.

name: Judge which measure of centre best represents a data set
description: judge whether the mean or the median gives the most representative picture of a data set, and justify the choice - particularly with regard to how outliers (extreme values) affect the mean more than the median.
instruction: Give the student a data set (or the measures of centre for it) where the mean and the median differ clearly, ideally because of a single extreme value, and ask them to judge and justify which measure of centre best represents the data.

name: Evaluate a claim about a distribution
description: evaluate a claim about a distribution based on stated measures of centre and spread, decide whether the claim is necessarily true, and where relevant support the answer with a counterexample.
instruction: Present a claim about one of two distributions (based on stated measures of centre and spread) and ask the student to decide whether the claim necessarily holds, with justification - constructing a counterexample data set where that helps.

name: Read lengths and distances in a coordinate system
description: read off the coordinates of points in a coordinate system and use them to determine lengths such as bases, heights and side lengths in a figure.
instruction: Show the student a simple figure drawn in a coordinate system with some coordinates marked, and ask them to determine the lengths (base, height, side length) needed for further calculation.

name: Use the area formula for a triangle
description: use the formula for the area of a triangle (half the base times the height) to determine the area of a triangle drawn in a coordinate system.
instruction: Show the student a triangle drawn in a coordinate system and ask them to determine its area.

name: Use the area formula for a trapezium
description: use the formula for the area of a trapezium, or alternatively split the figure into known parts (e.g. a rectangle and a triangle), to determine the area of a quadrilateral drawn in a coordinate system.
instruction: Show the student a trapezium-shaped (or otherwise composite) quadrilateral drawn in a coordinate system and ask them to determine the area, ideally by two different methods (the trapezium formula and splitting the figure up).

name: Use the area formula for a circle
description: use the formula for the area of a circle (π·r²) to calculate the area given the radius or the diameter.
instruction: Give the student the radius or the diameter of a circle and ask them to calculate the area.

name: Determine the area of a circular sector and of composite circular figures
description: determine the area of a circular sector, and use addition or subtraction of known areas to find the area of a composite figure made up of parts of a circle.
instruction: Show the student a figure made up of a circular sector, possibly with a piece cut away, drawn in a coordinate system, and ask them to determine the area of the figure.

name: Use Pythagoras' theorem
description: use Pythagoras' theorem to find an unknown side in a right-angled triangle when the two other sides are known.
instruction: Give the student a right-angled triangle in which two of the sides are known (leg-leg or leg-hypotenuse) and ask them to find the third side using Pythagoras' theorem.

name: Convert between units of volume
description: convert between units of volume such as mm³, cm³, m³ and litres, and combine this with converting units of length before a volume calculation.
instruction: Give the student a volume in one unit (mm³, cm³, m³ or litres) and ask them to convert it to another, stated unit - possibly combined with a length conversion before the volume calculation itself.

name: Calculate the volume of a right prism
description: calculate the volume of a right prism (e.g. a block or a layer with a given cross-section) by multiplying length, width and height/thickness, converting units correctly along the way.
instruction: Give the student the measurements (length, width, height/thickness) of a right prism in different units, and ask them to calculate the volume in a stated unit (e.g. cubic metres).

name: Calculate the volume of a cone
description: use the volume formula for a cone (V=⅓·π·r²·h) to calculate the volume given the diameter or radius and the height, and use the result to judge whether a quantity is sufficient in a practical setting.
instruction: Give the student the diameter (or radius) and the height of a cone-shaped heap or object, and ask them to calculate the volume, ideally with a follow-up about whether the volume is enough compared with another stated volume.

name: Solve a linear equation
description: solve a linear equation with one unknown.
instruction: Give the student a simple linear equation with one unknown and ask them to solve it.

name: Solve a factorised equation using the zero-product property
description: solve an equation given in factorised form by using the fact that a product is zero if and only if at least one of the factors is zero.
instruction: Give the student an equation of the form (expression)·(expression)=0 and ask them to find all the solutions.

name: Solve a system of equations algebraically
description: solve a linear system of equations with two unknowns algebraically, for example by substitution or by elimination.
instruction: Give the student a linear system of equations with two unknowns and ask them to solve it algebraically, showing the method clearly.

name: Set up and solve a system of equations from a word problem
description: translate a practical situation with several unknown quantities (two or three) into a system of equations, and solve it algebraically.
instruction: Give the student a word problem in which two or three people buy different combinations of the same goods for stated totals, or a comparable situation with two unknown quantities (e.g. the weight of two types of sack given the number of each and a stated total weight), and ask them to set up and solve the system of equations.

name: Linear function, gradient and constant term
description: A linear function can be written in the form y=ax+b, and knows what the gradient a and the constant term b mean.

name: Draw the graph of a linear function
description: draw the graph of a linear function given in equation form, for example by finding where it crosses the axes or by setting up a table of values.
instruction: Give the student a linear equation (e.g. in the form ax+by=c) and ask them to draw the graph by hand in a coordinate system.

name: Solve a system of equations graphically
description: solve a linear system of equations graphically by drawing both lines in the same coordinate system and reading off the point of intersection.
instruction: Give the student a linear system of equations and ask them to solve it graphically, with the point of intersection clearly marked.

name: Basic programming concepts
description:
Variable: a name given a value, which can be updated as the program runs.
List: several values under one name, each with a position.
Loop: repeats code - a for loop once per element, a while loop for as long as a condition holds.
Built-in functions: ready-made functions such as len(), which gives the number of elements, and sum(), which gives their total.

name: Interpret a short Python program
description: read a short Python program - with lists and simple built-in functions, or with a loop (for/while) that simulates something over time, e.g. a financial plan - follow the calculation step by step, and explain what the calculated and printed values represent in context.
instruction: Show the student a short Python program (without running it) - either one that calculates a quantity from a list of numbers, or one that uses a while or for loop to simulate something over time (e.g. withdrawals from an account that earns interest) - and ask them to explain what the printed values tell us.

name: Evaluate powers on a calculator
description: use a handheld calculator to evaluate expressions involving powers, including powers with decimal exponents and nth roots.
instruction: Give the student a range of expressions involving powers, including ones with a decimal exponent and an nth root, and ask them to evaluate them on the calculator.

name: Exponential function
description: An exponential function of the form f(x)=b·a^x describes a quantity that changes by a fixed growth factor a per unit of time, where b is the starting value.

name: Find the growth factor per period from a long-run change
description: determine the annual (periodic) growth factor when a known percentage change happens over several periods taken together, by taking the nth root of the growth factor for the whole period.
instruction: Give the student a description of a quantity that changes by a given percentage over a given number of periods taken together (e.g. halves every six years), and ask them to find the annual growth factor using a calculator.

name: Set up an exponential model
description: set up an exponential model f(x)=b·a^x from a written description of a starting value and a percentage or periodic change, and explain each step of the derivation.
instruction: Give the student a written situation with a starting value and information about a periodic percentage change, and ask them to show how a stated exponential model can be derived from that information.

name: Find the average change per unit of time
description: use an exponential function to calculate the average change per unit of time over a given interval, by evaluating function values on a calculator and dividing the difference by the length of the interval.
instruction: Give the student an exponential model and an interval, and ask them to calculate the average change per unit of time over that interval using a calculator.

name: Build an exponential model by regression
description: use regression on a handheld calculator to find an exponential model f(x)=a·b^x that fits a data set, and document the procedure.
instruction: Give the student a data set (e.g. a table of time against a quantity that grows or declines), and ask them to use the regression function on the calculator to find an exponential model, documenting the procedure.

name: Solve an exponential equation
description: solve an equation of the form a·b^x=c for x using a handheld calculator (e.g. an equation solver or logarithms), and interpret the answer in the context the task describes.
instruction: Give the student an exponential model and a stated function value, and ask them to find the corresponding x-value using a calculator, and to interpret the answer in context (e.g. «after how many months...»).

name: Percentage points versus percentage change
description:
Percentage points: the difference between two percentages. From 20 % to 25 % is a rise of 5 percentage points.
Percentage change: how much the share has changed relative to where it started. The same rise is an increase of 25 %.

name: Tell percentage points from percentage change
description: decide which of the two a given statement reports, work out both for the same figures, and explain how a claim becomes misleading when they are confused.

name: Compare data from two or more points in time
description: compare data sets from two or more points in time (e.g. proportions given as percentages), calculate the relevant changes and differences with a correct distinction between percentage points and percentage change, and put the comparisons into words.
instruction: Give the student two or more tables of comparable data from different points in time, and ask them to calculate and describe the most interesting changes, using percentage points and percentage change correctly.

name: Choose and produce a suitable chart
description: choose a type of chart (e.g. a bar chart, a pie chart or a line graph) that suits a given set of data, produce the chart, and justify the choice.
instruction: Give the student a set of data and ask them to choose and sketch a suitable type of chart, with a justification for the choice.

name: Present findings from a set of data
description: carry out relevant calculations and comparisons on a set of data, choose suitable charts, and put together a short presentation of the findings for an audience.
instruction: Give the student a composite set of data (two or more tables works well) and ask them to carry out calculations, produce charts and put together a short presentation of the most important findings.

name: Annuity loan
description: An annuity loan has the same instalment throughout the repayment period. The interest is calculated on the outstanding balance and shrinks each period, while the principal part is whatever is left of the instalment and therefore grows - the sum stays the same every time.

name: Calculate the interest and principal parts of one instalment
description: for a given outstanding balance, interest rate and instalment, calculate the interest part and the principal part of one payment, and then find the new outstanding balance.
instruction: Give the student an outstanding balance, an interest rate per period and an instalment, and ask them to work out the interest part, the principal part and the new outstanding balance for one period, using a calculator.

name: Set up a repayment schedule period by period
description: set up a repayment schedule covering several periods by repeating the calculation of interest, principal and new outstanding balance period by period, using a handheld calculator (for example its answer/repeat function) or a table drawn up by hand.
instruction: Give the student the loan amount, the interest rate and the instalment, and ask them to set up a repayment schedule for the first 4-5 periods by repeating the calculation period by period on a calculator. Make it clear that this is to be done without a spreadsheet - CAS software and spreadsheets (computer tools) are not permitted aids in Part 2, only a handheld calculator (which may well have graphing built in - that is not the problem).

name: Serial loan
description: A serial loan repays the same amount of principal every period. The interest is calculated on the outstanding balance and falls steadily, so the instalment is largest at the start and gets smaller throughout - unlike an annuity loan, where the instalment is fixed.

name: Calculate the fixed principal repayment on a serial loan
description: calculate the fixed principal repayment on a serial loan by dividing the loan amount by the number of periods.
instruction: Give the student the loan amount and the repayment period (number of periods) for a serial loan, and ask them to calculate the fixed principal repayment.

name: Calculate the instalment and the interest part on a serial loan
description: for a serial loan, calculate the interest part and the instalment for a given period from the outstanding balance at that point, and compare how the instalment changes with different repayment periods.
instruction: Give the student the loan amount, the interest rate and the repayment period for a serial loan, and ask them to calculate the instalment for one or more stated periods - and where relevant to compare it with the instalment under a different repayment period.

name: Compare different saving or investment options
description: calculate the final value of several different saving or investment options (e.g. a single overall percentage change, a fixed annual interest rate over several years, or several different percentage changes year by year) and set them out side by side for comparison.
instruction: Give the student the same starting amount placed in two or three different saving or investment options with different return information, and ask them to calculate the final amount for each option and bring the results together in one overview.

name: Find the original number from a percentage
description: given a percentage of a number together with either that part itself or the rest (the complement) as a count, work out what the original (whole) number is.
instruction: Give the student a percentage and a corresponding quantity, either directly (e.g. «40 % of a team is 12 people») or via the complement (e.g. «88 % take part, 3 do not»), and ask them to find the total number. Pure calculation, a single numerical answer.

name: Argue that «a % of b» and «b % of a» are equal
description: argue why «a per cent of b» always gives the same answer as «b per cent of a», by showing that both expressions amount to (a·b)/100.
instruction: Give the student several pairs of percentage questions set up as «a % of b?» and «b % of a?» (e.g. 10 % of 50 and 50 % of 10), and ask them to explain - algebraically if they can - why the two questions in each pair always give the same answer.

name: Use the circumference formula for a circle and find an arc length
description: use the formula for the circumference of a circle (2·π·r) to calculate the circumference given the radius or the diameter, and calculate the arc length of a circular sector as a fraction of the whole circumference.
instruction: Give the student the radius or the diameter of a circle and ask them to calculate the circumference, where relevant combined with finding the arc length of a given sector (e.g. a semicircle) as a fraction of the whole circumference.

name: Determine the perimeter of a composite figure
description: determine the perimeter of a composite or unfamiliar figure - for example a semicircle, or a triangle where only the base and the height are given - by adding up side lengths and where necessary arc lengths, and using Pythagoras' theorem to find missing side lengths.
instruction: Give the student two figures to compare, e.g. a semicircle and an isosceles triangle where only the base and the height are given, and ask them to find the perimeter of each - where the sloping sides of the triangle must first be found with Pythagoras' theorem - and to decide which figure has the greater perimeter.

name: Similar triangles
description: Two triangles are similar when their angles are equal in pairs and their sides are proportional, and can explain why two triangles are similar - for example from vertically opposite angles and parallel lines, or from given information about the angles.

name: Use similarity to find an unknown length
description: use the similarity of two triangles to set up a proportion between corresponding sides, and solve for an unknown length.
instruction: Give the student a situation involving two similar triangles (e.g. a sketch with known and unknown distances, or a word problem about measuring a distance across a river or an obstacle), and ask them to set up a proportion between corresponding sides and solve for the unknown length.

name: Use area scaling under similarity
description: use the relationship between the scale factor for lengths and the scale factor for areas - the ratio of the areas is the square of the ratio of the lengths - to find unknown side lengths in a similar figure when the area is given.
instruction: Give the student a figure (e.g. a right-angled triangle) with known side lengths, and ask them to find the side lengths of a similar figure with a stated area, using the fact that the ratio of the areas is the square of the ratio of the lengths between the figures.

name: Determine the area of a regular polygon
description: determine the area of a regular polygon (e.g. a regular hexagon) by splitting it into congruent triangles from the centre and using the area formula for a triangle, where necessary with Pythagoras' theorem to find the height of each triangle.
instruction: Give the student the side length of a regular polygon (e.g. a hexagon), and ask them to determine the area by splitting the figure into congruent triangles from the centre and adding up their areas.

name: Frustum of a cone
description: A frustum is a cone whose top has been cut off by a cut parallel to the base, and its volume can be calculated by subtracting the volume of the small cone that was cut off from the volume of the original, whole cone.

name: Calculate the volume of a frustum of a cone
description: calculate the volume of a frustum by setting up a whole cone, using the similarity between the whole cone and the top cone that is cut away to find the height of the top cone, and subtracting the volume of the top cone from the volume of the whole cone.
instruction: Give the student practical requirements for a frustum (e.g. measurements for the base, the top face and the maximum height of an object to be shaped), and ask them to propose suitable measurements, draw a sketch with those measurements marked, and calculate the volume by starting from a whole cone and subtracting the top cone that is cut away.

name: Estimate the median from a grouped frequency table
description: estimate the median of a grouped data set given as a frequency table (without a cumulative frequency graph), by determining which class the median falls in and using linear interpolation under an assumption of an even distribution within that class.
instruction: Give the student a grouped frequency table and ask them to estimate the median by finding which class the middle observation falls in and interpolating within that class, and ask them to state explicitly the assumption of an even distribution that the estimate rests on.

name: Histograms with frequency density and unequal class widths
description: In a histogram whose classes have unequal widths, frequency density (frequency divided by class width) is used on the y-axis, so that the area of each bar - not its height - corresponds to the frequency of that class.

name: Read off and calculate from a histogram with frequency density
description: read a histogram with frequency density on the y-axis and classes of unequal width, calculate the frequency of a class as height times width, and use this to determine counts, relative frequencies, the mean and the median for all or part of the data.
instruction: Show the student a histogram with frequency density on the y-axis and classes of unequal width, and ask them to argue for or evaluate several claims that require working out the number of observations, the relative frequency, the mean and/or the median for all or part of the data.

name: Reason about how the median changes when a data point is added
description: reason about whether the median of a data set necessarily changes when a new data point is added, based on whether the number of observations was originally odd or even.
instruction: Give the student a data set and a claim that the median will (necessarily) change if a new, unknown data point is added, and ask them to judge whether the claim is correct, with a justification tied to whether the number of observations is odd or even.

name: Find the value that must be added to reach a desired mean
description: given a data set and a desired mean for that data set extended by one new value, work out which value must be added to achieve that mean, and judge whether the value is reasonable in context.
instruction: Give the student a data set and a claimed mean for the data set if one new value were added, and ask them to work out which value would then have to be added, and to judge whether that value is reasonable or even possible in the context the task describes.

name: Construct a data set that matches stated measures of centre and spread
description: construct an example of a data set that meets given requirements on measures of centre (median, mean) and spread (standard deviation), relative to another given data set.
instruction: Give the student a data set and a description of how another data set's median, mean and standard deviation compare with it (higher/lower/smaller), and ask them to construct a concrete example of that other data set and show with a calculator that it matches the description.

name: Exponential model with a limiting value
description: A model of the form f(x)=b·a^x+c describes a quantity developing exponentially towards a limiting value (asymptote) c rather than towards zero, and can explain what b, a and c mean in such a setting.

name: Calculate with an exponential model that has a limiting value
description: use a model of the form f(x)=b·a^x+c to solve equations for x with a calculator, and judge whether a given target can ever be reached by comparing it with the model's limiting value c.
instruction: Give the student a model of the form f(x)=b·a^x+c (e.g. emissions falling towards a floor) and ask them to solve an equation for x with a calculator, and then to judge whether a stated target can be reached at all according to the model, by reasoning about the limiting value c.

name: Interpret a Python program that solves equations by iteration
description: read a Python program that solves an equation or a system of equations numerically by testing (iterating over) x-values in a given interval and checking a condition such as f(x)==g(x), explain the strategy behind the approach, and make the changes needed for the program to solve another, comparable system of equations.
instruction: Show the student a short Python program that defines two functions and loops through an interval of x-values to find where the two functions are equal, and ask them to explain the strategy - and then to adapt the program (the function expressions and/or the interval) to solve another, similar system of equations.

name: Decide whether a loan is an annuity loan or a serial loan
description: decide whether a loan is an annuity loan or a serial loan from a repayment schedule (table or chart), by judging whether the principal repayment or the instalment is constant from period to period.
instruction: Give the student a repayment schedule (a table or a bar chart) showing the instalment, the interest and the principal repayment per period, and ask them to decide whether the loan is an annuity loan or a serial loan, justified by what stays constant across the repayment period.

name: Determine the loan amount and the interest rate from a repayment schedule
description: from a repayment schedule (a table or chart showing the instalment, the interest, the principal repayment and possibly the outstanding balance per period), determine the original loan amount and the interest rate per period, whether the loan is an annuity loan or a serial loan.
instruction: Give the student a repayment schedule (a table or a chart), and ask them to determine the original loan amount (e.g. by adding up the principal repayments or reading off the first outstanding balance) and the interest rate per period (e.g. from the interest part and the outstanding balance in the first period).

name: Equity requirement on a mortgage
description: Norwegian banks normally require at least 15 % equity on a mortgage, so that the maximum loan is 85 % of the price of the property, and can use this to work out the equity needed or the maximum loan.

name: Gross pay and net pay
description: Net income is gross income minus tax and any other deductions (e.g. pension saving and trade union dues), and the deductions are normally calculated as percentages of the gross income.

name: Calculate net income from gross pay and deductions
description: calculate a person's net income from their gross pay and stated percentage deductions (tax, pension, trade union dues and so on), including where relevant overtime pay calculated from a given hourly rate and a percentage premium.
instruction: Give the student a fixed monthly salary or an hourly rate, where relevant with a given number of overtime hours and a percentage overtime premium, together with percentage deductions (tax, pension and the like), and ask them to calculate the net income for one month.

name: Assess personal finances against a budget
description: set up a simple household budget by comparing net income with fixed expenses (e.g. loan costs, insurance and a reference budget for living costs), and judge whether the finances come out in surplus or deficit.
instruction: Give the student a net income and fixed expenses (e.g. a reference budget, a loan cost and insurance), and ask them to set up an overall budget and judge whether the person can afford a given expense (e.g. a mortgage), with the reasoning backed by numbers.

name: Coordinate system
description: A coordinate system consists of two perpendicular axes (the x-axis and the y-axis) that make it possible to give points, lengths and graphs as numerical values.

name: Outstanding balance
description: The outstanding balance is the amount left to pay on a loan at a given point in time, and the interest in each period is calculated on the outstanding balance - not on the original loan amount.

name: Instalment period
description: An instalment period is a fixed payment period on a loan (monthly, for example), and each period pays some interest and some principal.

name: Interest rate
description: The interest rate is the interest charged per period, and tells this apart from the total interest paid over the whole life of the loan.

name: Point of intersection
description: The point of intersection between two graphs is the point where the graphs have the same x-value and the same y-value, and this point corresponds to the solution of the associated system of equations.

name: Proportion
description: A proportion is a statement that two ratios are equal, and can use this to set up the fact that corresponding sides in similar figures are in the same ratio.
